fix: In 'inserted near base of X', the place belongs to X. The 'towards' slot keeps only the bare word 'base' and loses 'of perianth lobes'.
reason: The stamens are inserted near the base of the perianth lobes. The target 'plant organ base' (FLOPO_0985024) does not say whose base it is, so the stamen's own base could be meant.

fix: 'not conspicuously X' negates how visible X is, not X itself. Read it as 'X, inconspicuous', not as 'not X'.
reason: The petiole may be articulated but not visibly so. The annotation says the petiole is not jointed.
The stem is about 4 cm long.
'Shrubs or trees' gives both habits as alternatives.
'Arbuste' means shrub. The 'or small tree' alternative later in the text is missing, but what is said is true.
There are 2 glumes per male spikelet. The male-spikelet context is lost, but 2 glumes per spikelet holds generally.

fix: In 'A- or B-C' (a hyphen left hanging), C belongs to both parts: 'A-C or B-C'. Do not split it into A, C.
reason: 'grey- or purple-brown' means grey-brown or purple-brown. The values 'gray' and 'brown' are not what the flora says.
The leaflets are glabrous above, on the upper (adaxial) side, as the scope slot gives.
There are 3 or 4 stigmas.

fix: 'attenuate at the base' should switch the bearer to the base, as in the 'place on the part' pattern. In the plain stratum the place is dropped.
reason: Only the base is attenuate. The apex is described separately (long-attenuate/subcaudate), so 'the whole blade is attenuate' misstates it.
'Subsuperior' means nearly superior, so 'approximately superior' fits.
The older branches are glabrous; the 'old' context is kept.

fix: In fern descriptions, 'aréoles' are the meshes of the vein network, not cactus areoles (areole bud).
reason: For Antrophyum the open marginal areoles are vein meshes near the frond margin.

fix: 'veins N on each side of the midrib' counts lateral veins of the blade, not tissue-level vascular bundles.
reason: These are the leaflet's lateral (secondary) veins.
The species is monoecious.
The style is yellowish green.
The blade base is attenuate.
The bracts of the fruiting catkin are pilose at the base.

fix: 'pilose' on a leaf surface is a pilosity value. PATO 'pubescent hair' is a quality of a hair, not of a hairy surface.
reason: The leaflets are densely pilose on both sides when young. The young context is right.
The leaves are oblong or oblanceolate.
The flower sides range from straight to sigmoid, sometimes jaggedly; the 'sometimes' qualifier is kept.

fix: 'boat-shaped spathes absent' denies only spathes, not all bracts. Map spathe to inflorescence bract and keep the shape word.
reason: The inflorescences sit in the axils of reduced leaves, which act as bracts. Only boat-shaped spathes are absent.
The branchlets are glabrate (glabrescent).
The inflorescence has many flowers.
Annual or perennial.
There are 5–7 lateral veins on each side of the midrib.

fix: 'not X beneath/at Y' keeps the place Y in the scope of the negation.
reason: Only the part beneath the mouth is not constricted. The capsule is 'sharply contracted' toward the seta, so a bare 'capsule not constricted' overstates it.
The calyx is about 1 cm at flowering; the flowering-stage context is kept.
The pomes are orange-red when young.
The leaf blade is oblong to elliptic.
